homebrew.name: rooted-city
homebrew.title: The Rooted City
homebrew.credit: Original homebrew for a D&D 5e campaign.

materials.name: Thornling Spine
materials.desc: A needle-sharp, hand-length thorn, dark as old iron at the tip and green at the root. Fletchers prize it: the tip barbs backward and lodges in a wound.

materials.name: Loamborn Clay
materials.desc: A scoop of fine, dark, fertile clay that smells of rain and still holds the shape of whatever pressed it last. Potters and herbalists pay extra for a lump with something embedded in it: a button, a bead, a bone-chip.

materials.name: Rootwolf Pelt
materials.desc: A grey-green pelt that rustles like dry leaves and sheds a faint scent of cut grass. Rangers line cloaks with it because it muffles the wearer's tread.

materials.name: Rootwolf Sinew
materials.desc: Long cords of wiry, bark-fibred tendon. They bind tighter as they dry and make excellent bowstrings and lashings.

materials.name: Bramble-Boar Tusk
materials.desc: A curved, ridged tusk with a thorny knot at the base, as dense as seasoned oak and twice as heavy as ivory.

materials.name: Cobblevine Tendril
materials.desc: A silver-green vine as supple as rope and surprisingly strong. It grips whatever it is wound around, and remembers the shape of the last thing it held.

materials.name: Charnel Loam
materials.desc: Black, greasy compost threaded with bone-dust and fine white roots. It carries rot and the memory of rot, and alchemists use it as a reagent for wards against sickness (and, less kindly, to spread it).

materials.name: Hushed-Alder Bark
materials.desc: Silver-grey bark, cool to the touch, which swallows sound. A strip held to the ear mutes the world, and a sheet of it laid under a floor stops footsteps carrying.

materials.name: Canopy-Lurker Pelt
materials.desc: A tawny pelt patterned like moss on bark, stiff along the spine. It hardly reflects light and sheds rain, which is why scouts and burglars covet it.

materials.name: Alder-Dryad Sap
materials.desc: A thin, amber sap that smells of green apples and warm bread. It heals gently and makes the drinker feel unreasonably fond of the nearest tree.

materials.name: Mourning-Elk Antler
materials.desc: A branch of white antler wound with pale roots. Hold it to the ear and you will hear a name, someone's, called softly and often. It is cold in the hand even in summer.

materials.name: Elk Memory-Bloom
materials.desc: A small pale flower that grows from the crown of the antlers. It wilts within a day but, while fresh, it lets the holder recall a single lost thing with perfect clarity.

materials.name: Evergreen Signet
materials.desc: A small silver livery-pin stamped with an oak leaf and apple. Pawnbrokers pay modestly. Anyone who recognises the crest will pay in other ways.

materials.name: Dawnbriar Arrowhead
materials.desc: A thorn grown into the shape of an arrowhead and hardened by spring-light, its tip beaded with a pale green venom that burns slowly.

materials.name: Huntsman's Horn-Reed
materials.desc: The reed from a fey hunting horn: long, pale, humming faintly, and faintly distasteful to anything with prey instincts.

materials.name: Ward-Iron Ingot
materials.desc: A dense, green-streaked bar of founders' iron-bark alloy. It is cold, heavy, and rings a half-note lower than steel. Anything made from it resists being undone.

materials.name: Ward Core
materials.desc: A fist-sized knot of bronze and living-grain wood that hums with an old, patient purpose. It was made to hold something in, and holds it still.

materials.name: Sentinel Heartwood
materials.desc: Dark red heartwood, dense as stone and warm as skin, with a grain that moves slowly if you watch it long enough.

materials.name: Greenmother's Heartseed
materials.desc: A fat, golden seed the size of a plum, warm and faintly pulsing. Planted in sound earth, it will become something that does not stop growing.

materials.name: Living Heartwood Plank
materials.desc: A plank of heartwood that has not entirely forgotten it is alive. It mends small cracks overnight and refuses to rot.

materials.name: Fringe Nettle
materials.desc: A broad, dark-veined nettle that springs from cracked cobbles in the overgrown streets. Its sting is mild and its sap knits flesh surprisingly fast.

materials.name: Memory Root
materials.desc: A pale, knotted root found where old cellars and graves have been split open by growth. Chewed, it brings back things you thought you had forgotten.

materials.name: Threadwalker Silk
materials.desc: Pale, fine silk spun by something that walks along the seams between places. It is surprisingly strong and never quite lies where you left it.

materials.name: Seamstress's Thread
materials.desc: A single strand, longer than it looks and thinner than hair, that does not tear. Pulled taut, it hums like a held breath.

materials.name: Seamstress's Bone Needle
materials.desc: A hand-long needle of pale bone with a sliver of silk in its eye. It can close a wound, and it can close a thin place between worlds.

materials.name: Drowned Legion Plate
materials.desc: Corroded plate from a drowned Hollowcrown legionary. Pitted, green and heavy, but the steel beneath is sound and still stamped with a unit number.

materials.name: Tribune's Seal
materials.desc: A bronze signet ring-seal from a drowned Hollowcrown officer, rimed with river-silt. It carries the weight of an order never rescinded.

materials.name: Thorn-Knight Briar-Plate
materials.desc: Overlapping plates of living thorn-wood that turn aside a blade and bristle at a grasp. They fade to grey in a week if cut from the wearer's armour.

materials.name: Frost-Silk Glove
materials.desc: A glove of cold-stitched frost-silk that never warms. Used once, it seals a bargain so that it cannot be broken without the breaker paying.

materials.name: Thornling Heart-Bud
materials.desc: A tight green knot from the core of a thornling, sticky and smelling of crushed rose-leaf. Cooks stuff roasts with it to keep them moist, and herbalists say it settles a weary body.

materials.name: Drudge Rootlets
materials.desc: Pale, finger-thick roots that served a loamborn drudge as sinews. Scrubbed of clay they cook like sweet parsnips and thicken any pottage.

materials.name: Rootwolf Meat
materials.desc: Lean, dark meat with a faint taste of resin and cut grass. Hung for a night it loses its sappiness and makes a fine pie or stew.

materials.name: Rootwolf Heart
materials.desc: A small, hard heart threaded with fine rootlets, which beats slowly for a minute after the kill. Poachers' cooks bake it into pies said to lighten the step.

materials.name: Bramble-Boar Haunch
materials.desc: A heavy hindquarter of marbled pork with a green tinge to the fat. Roasted slow under its own peeled briars, it feeds a whole street.

materials.name: Bramble-Boar Heart
materials.desc: A fist-and-a-half of dense, dark muscle with thorn-like ridges on its outer wall. Roasted inside the joint, it is believed to lend the boar's stubborn hide to whoever eats it.

materials.name: Cobblevine Sap
materials.desc: A slow, honey-coloured sap tapped from the thick stem of a cobblevine. It sets tacky as it cools, and cooks use it as a sticky, faintly sweet glaze.

materials.name: Hushed Alder Catkins
materials.desc: Long grey catkins shaken from a hushed alder; they fall without a sound. Baked into pastry or steeped, they make the eater's movements oddly quiet.

materials.name: Canopy Lurker Claws
materials.desc: Hooked, bark-brown claws that bite into timber and stone alike. Leatherworkers set them into climbing gloves and boot-spurs.

materials.name: Mourning-Elk Venison
materials.desc: Dark, fine-grained venison that smells faintly of autumn leaves. Those who eat it often dream of people they have lost, clearly and without pain.

materials.name: Mourning-Elk Heart
materials.desc: A great, heavy heart, cold to the touch and utterly silent. Cooked at wakes, it is said to steady the mind against grief and things that would break it.

materials.name: Threadwalker Legs
materials.desc: The long, jointed walking-legs of a threadwalker. Cracked like crab, the pale meat inside is sweet and sticky, and rooftop foragers swear it steadies a climbing hand.

materials.name: Pantry Preserves
materials.desc: A stoppered jar of fruit preserves from an old larder, carried in an apron pocket. Still sweet; cooks stretch it into tarts and glazes.

materials.name: Legion Hardtack
materials.desc: A wax-sealed ration tin of hard soldier's biscuit. About half the tins are still dry inside; soaked and broken into a pot, it makes a filling pottage.

materials.name: Sentinel Acorn
materials.desc: An acorn the size of a fist, red-brown and warm, dropped from a walking heartwood tree. Leached and roasted, its meat is dense, rich and famously fortifying.

materials.name: Cobble-Berries
materials.desc: Small, dark, tart berries on low brambles that fruit along kerbs and between paving stones. Bakers stretch them into tarts and jams; children eat them by the fistful.

materials.name: Gutter Chanterelles
materials.desc: Golden, apricot-scented mushrooms that crowd leaf-choked gutters and drains after rain. Good fried in fat; easily confused with the far less pleasant gutter cap.

materials.name: Windowsill Sorrel
materials.desc: A sour, lemony leaf that has spread from old window boxes across sills, ledges and balconies. Wilted into a pan it brightens any dish.

materials.name: Belltower Moss
materials.desc: A soft, grey-gold moss that grows only on bell-frames and louvres where bells rang for generations; it trembles at the faintest sound. Brewed into broth, it sharpens the ear.

materials.name: Rafter Honeycomb
materials.desc: Dark, flower-heavy comb from wild bees nesting in the rafters of roofless houses. The honey is thick and bitter-sweet; the wax is good for sealing jars.

materials.name: Paving-Crack Acorns
materials.desc: Acorns from the young oaks that have heaved up the city's paving. Leached in running water and ground, they make a coarse, nutty flour for crusts and flatbreads.

materials.name: Chapel Mint
materials.desc: A tall, purple-stemmed mint run wild from old cloister and chapel herb-beds. Cooks use it to lift fatty meat and to make stale water drinkable.

materials.name: Cellar Morels
materials.desc: Honeycomb-capped mushrooms that sprout on old barrels and beams in root-split cellars. Earthy and meaty, they fry well and dry better.

materials.name: Fountain Cress
materials.desc: A peppery watercress choking the basins of silted fountains and horse-troughs. Eaten raw or wilted; wash it well.

materials.name: Briar Hips
materials.desc: The fat red hips of wild briars that have swallowed the city's hedges and railings. Sweetest after the first frost, they make glazes, syrups and a warming tea.

items.name: Salve of Rootknit
items.effect: A green, grassy-smelling salve spread over a wound. It knits skin in moments, restoring 2d4+2 hit points and closing one bleeding or lingering cut.

recipe.lore: Nettle sap is a sharp knitting agent; moss softens it and beeswax holds it as a salve that clings to a wound.

items.name: Briarbarb Arrows
items.effect: Arrows tipped with thornling spines. A hit leaves a barb in the wound: the target takes an extra 1d4 poison damage at the start of its next turn unless it spends an action pulling the barb out.

recipe.lore: The spine's backward barb does the work; wax holds the head so that it does not simply fall out in flight.

items.name: Thornguard Cloak
items.effect: A cloak lined with rootwolf pelt and sewn through with thorns. While wearing it you have advantage on Stealth checks in wooded or overgrown places, and a creature that hits you with a melee attack takes 1d4 piercing damage.

recipe.lore: Rootwolf fur hides the wearer; the alder essence hushes the step; the thorns remember which hand reached for the cloak.

items.name: Staff of the Hush
items.attune: by a druid, ranger or spellcaster
items.effect: A pale quarterstaff of alder wood. It has 3 charges and regains 1d3 at dawn. As an action, spend 1 charge to cast silence (no concentration needed for the first minute). On a roll of 1 after spending the last charge, the staff turns to grey ash.

recipe.lore: The bark already swallows sound; the moss deepens it; the wax seals the quiet into the staff.

items.name: Wand of Grieving Echoes
items.effect: A wand of white antler. It has 3 charges and regains 1d3 at dawn. Spend 1 charge as an action: a creature within 30 feet must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom save or hear a dead loved one calling it by name, taking 2d6 psychic damage and having disadvantage on attack rolls until the end of its next turn.

recipe.lore: The antler remembers the voices it carried, the bloom lets the holder choose which one to call, and silver gives it a clear tone.

items.name: Ward-Iron Shield
items.effect: A heavy shield of green-streaked iron. It grants +1 AC like a +1 shield, and you have advantage on saving throws against spells and effects from fey. A fey or plant creature that hits you with a melee attack takes 1d6 force damage.

recipe.lore: The core was made to hold something in; reforged into a shield it holds things out, and the ward-iron carries the old Founders' purpose.

items.name: Heartseed Lantern
items.effect: A lantern holding a living seed that glows a soft green. It sheds light in a 30-foot radius; nonmagical difficult terrain made of plants doesn't slow you or allies in the light. Once per day, as an action, you can cast plant growth from it.

recipe.lore: A heartseed holds a forest in a shell; the plank frames it, the glass lets the light out, and the sap keeps it from sprouting through the lantern.

items.name: Loamborn Clay Poultice
items.effect: A jar of cool, fertile clay wrapped in a leaf. Applied over 1 minute it restores 2d4+2 hit points and ends one poison condition. It spoils after 3 days.

recipe.lore: Clay draws out poison, nettle knits the wound and wax keeps the clay from drying in the jar.

items.name: Alder-Bark Tea
items.effect: A pouch of brewed grey bark. For 1 hour you have advantage on saving throws against being frightened and on Wisdom (Insight) checks.

recipe.lore: The bark quiets the mind, honey carries the flavour and herbs keep the quiet from turning bitter.

items.name: Briar-Lance of the Court
items.effect: A +1 lance of dark wood wrapped in living briar. Once per day when you hit, the target must succeed on a DC 14 Strength save or be pulled 10 feet toward you.

recipe.lore: The knight's living briar grips the wood, the spines remember their prey and the thread binds it all.

items.name: Cloak of Thin Places
items.effect: A cloak stitched with seamstress-thread. Once per day, as a bonus action, you can step through a seam: teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see that is in shadow or among roots, webs or hollow trunks.

recipe.lore: A single strand of the Seamstress's thread knows where every seam is; the silk gives it grip, and silver wire holds the stitch.

items.name: Glove of the Sealed Word
items.effect: A cold-stitched glove. Once per day, as an action, you can seal an agreement with a willing creature by clasping hands: until the agreement is fulfilled, either party that knowingly breaks it takes 4d6 psychic damage and has disadvantage on Charisma checks for 24 hours.

recipe.lore: The frost-silk remembers the cold of a bargain, silver wire keeps the clasp honest and thread ties the terms to the wearer.

items.name: Cobble-Berry Tart
items.effect: A dark, tart-sweet pie in a ground-acorn crust. A slice counts as a meal, and sharing it softens people: for 1 hour you gain a +1 bonus to Charisma (Persuasion) checks against a creature that ate a slice with you.

recipe.lore: Every street with a working oven bakes these by late summer; the acorn crust is gritty, the berries stain everything, and nobody ever turns a slice down.

items.name: Gutter-and-Sill Fry
items.effect: A sizzling pan of street mushrooms wilted with sorrel and cress. A plate counts as a meal, and the sour greens sharpen you: you gain a +1 bonus to the next Wisdom (Perception) check you make within 1 hour.

recipe.lore: Picked from the drain, the sill and the fountain on the walk home; the only real skill is knowing a chanterelle from a gutter cap.

items.name: Drowned-Ration Pottage
items.effect: A thick soldier's pottage of soaked hardtack, roots and whatever meat the street gave up. A bowl counts as a day's food and warms you through: you have advantage on the next Constitution saving throw you make against cold weather before your next long rest.

recipe.lore: The biscuit comes out of a dead soldier's tin as often as not; soak it an hour, boil it with roots and mint, and it is as good as the day it was baked.

items.name: Rootwolf Pie
items.effect: A dense, peppery pie of rootwolf meat with the heart baked into the middle. For 8 hours you have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to move quietly through overgrown streets, woods or rubble.

components.label: Quiet-footed ingredient (rootwolf heart or hushed alder catkins)

recipe.lore: Poachers' wives bake the heart whole in the centre so whoever cuts the pie gets the quiet first; catkins do the same job when the wolf got away.

items.name: Bramble-Boar Briar Roast
items.effect: A haunch roasted under its own peeled briars and glazed with vine-sap, enough for a street. Up to six creatures who share it within an hour gain this benefit for 8 hours: the first time you are reduced to half your hit point maximum or fewer, you gain temporary hit points equal to 1d4 + your proficiency bonus.

components.label: Stubborn heart (bramble-boar heart or sentinel acorn)

recipe.lore: The heart goes in the belly of the joint with a thornling bud for moisture; hunters say you shrug off the first bad blow the morning after, the way the boar shrugs off the briars.

items.name: Belltower Broth
items.effect: A thin, grey-gold broth that leaves a faint ringing in the ears. For 8 hours you have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing.

recipe.lore: Night watchers climb for the moss because it still shivers at a bell rung streets away; simmered gently, it hands that shiver on to whoever drinks it.

items.name: Rooftop Threadwalker Skewers
items.effect: Cracked threadwalker legs grilled with a sticky vine-sap glaze. For 8 hours you have advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks made to climb.

recipe.lore: Rooftop foragers grill the legs over a chimney-pot fire; the meat is sweet as crab and leaves your fingers tacky long after you have licked them clean.

items.name: Elk-Wake Remembrance Stew
items.effect: A dark, quiet stew served at wakes. For 8 hours you have resistance to psychic damage, and you have advantage on Intelligence checks made to recall something you have seen, heard or read.

recipe.lore: The heart is simmered whole and in silence alongside memory-root; mourners say the stew lets you remember the dead clearly without the remembering hurting.

items.name: Lurker-Claw Climbing Gloves
items.effect: Leather gloves set with hooked canopy lurker claws. While wearing them you have advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks made to climb trees, timber and crumbling masonry, but you have disadvantage on checks that need fine finger-work.

recipe.lore: Each claw is sinew-lashed over a knuckle and set in vine-sap; the gloves grip bark the way the cat did, and they are miserable for buttoning a coat.

monsters.name: Thornling
monsters.blurb: A knee-high, hunch-backed clump of briars that rolls out of broken hedges in clutches to snag ankles and spit thorns.

harvest.note: Cut at the root while the thorn is still green, or it snaps.
A green knot at the core; split the clump with a knife before the thorns brown.

monsters.name: Loamborn Drudge
monsters.blurb: A barrel-chested figure of packed soil with roots for sinews, shaped from the forest's surplus power.

harvest.note: A DC 14 Nature check notices a bead, button or bone-chip embedded in the clay.
The pale roots that served as its sinews. Scrub off the clay before cooking.

monsters.name: Rootwolf
monsters.blurb: A lean, grey-green hound with bark-flecked flanks and a coat that rustles like leaves.

harvest.note: Skin in one piece, before the shoots in the fur wilt.
Lean and resinous; hang it overnight or it tastes of sap.
Take it quickly; it stops beating within the minute and spoils within the hour.

monsters.name: Bramble Boar
monsters.blurb: A pony-sized tusked boar whose back is sheathed in barbed briars instead of bristles.

harvest.note: Handle with gloves; the thorn-knot at the base punctures a careless hand.
Peel the briar-hide back first; the thorns run under the skin.
Reach in under the ribs with gloved hands; the heart wall is ridged and sharp.

monsters.name: Strangling Cobblevine
monsters.blurb: A silver-green vine hidden beneath paving that grips whatever steps within reach.

harvest.note: Tap the thick stem where it dives under the paving; it bleeds slowly for an hour.

monsters.name: Charnel Mound
monsters.blurb: A shambling heap of compost, ribs and rotting leaf-mould that drags itself from old graveyards.

harvest.note: Gloves and a cloth over the face. Untreated exposure risks disease.

monsters.name: Hushed Alder
monsters.blurb: A tall, slender, grey-barked tree with a face of knots that always looks about to speak, and the air around it is thick with silence.

harvest.note: Strip the bark only after a spoken apology; strips taken in anger are brittle.
Shake them down onto a cloth; catkins picked by hand turn brown and lose their quiet.

monsters.name: Canopy Lurker
monsters.blurb: A lean cat the size of a leopard with a pelt that has turned to bark and moss, waiting on high branches.

harvest.note: The pelt loses its camouflage if cut across the spine.
Draw them out with the toe-pads attached; they keep once dried.

monsters.name: Alder Dryad
monsters.blurb: A tree-nymph in a gown of leaf and white bark who guards her alder with cool courtesy.

harvest.note: Given freely or not at all. Sap taken from a slain dryad is spoiled and worth nothing.

monsters.name: The Mourning Elk
monsters.blurb: A towering stag with bone-white antlers wound with dead-leaf crowns, whispering the names of the dead.

harvest.note: Cut at the base while the voices are quiet.
Wilts within a day. Pluck it before the antler is cut.
Butcher it where it fell, and quietly; the meat sours if the carcass is dragged.
Take it within the hour. It is heavy as a stone and makes no sound when dropped.

monsters.name: Leashed Retainer
monsters.blurb: A servant in a noble house's livery, kept in service by a lesser Tithe and set to guard. Not harvestable beyond belongings.

harvest.note: A livery-pin. Their bodies are not harvestable.
A stoppered jar of preserves in an apron pocket. Their bodies are not harvestable.

monsters.name: Dawnbriar Huntsman
monsters.blurb: A lean, watchful fey in antler-mail with a willow bow and a horn that sounds like a dying stag.

harvest.note: The horn only yields its reed if the huntsman has not blown it in the last hour.

monsters.name: Iron Ward-Warden
monsters.blurb: A seven-foot suit of iron-bark plate with a hollow helm glowing faintly green, built to protect old chains.

harvest.note: Salvaging the plate without breaking it takes a day.
Pry it out before the glow fades, or it goes dull and inert.

monsters.name: Heartwood Sentinel
monsters.blurb: A colossal walking tree of dark red heartwood with a silver crown, standing guard at the centre of an old wood.

harvest.note: Needs a saw and a day; the grain fights the blade.
Gathered from the crown after it falls still; leach in running water before roasting.

monsters.name: Greenmother's Hand
monsters.blurb: An impossible, colossal hand of living wood and moss rising from the earth, guarding rather than killing.

harvest.note: Only lies in the palm once the Hand has gone still. Plant it in good earth.

monsters.name: Threadwalker
monsters.blurb: A spindly, many-legged spider that walks along seams and tears between places, trailing fine pale silk.

harvest.note: Cut the strands while the creature is still, or the silk slips away along the seam.
Only the long walking-legs are good; the body is bitter. Crack them like crab.

monsters.name: The Seamstress of Thin Places
monsters.blurb: A spider as large as a cottage, pale as chitin and dark as thread, that stitches the seam between this world and the Feywild shut.

harvest.note: Only given, never taken. A strand cut from an unwilling Seamstress comes away dull.
Lies in her foreleg's joint. Remove it with care; she will not forgive a careless hand.

monsters.name: Drowned Legionary
monsters.blurb: A drowned soldier in corroded Hollowcrown plate, weed hanging from every strap, still holding the ground it was ordered to hold.

harvest.note: A unit tag is stamped on the inside of the breastplate.
A wax-sealed ration tin in the belt-pouch; about half are still dry inside. The body is not food.

monsters.name: Drowned Tribune
monsters.blurb: A drowned Hollowcrown officer with a crest of waterweed and a cloak of silt, still asking for the relief column that never came.

harvest.note: It can be used to lay one drowned legionary to rest.
An officer's ration tin, better sealed than most. The body is not food.

monsters.name: Dawnbriar Thorn-Knight
monsters.blurb: A fey knight in plate of living briar, guarding a lord's word as closely as its own armour.

harvest.note: Cut while the armour still flowers; dead briar is brittle.

monsters.name: Castellan Ravel Evergreen
monsters.blurb: A silver-haired duellist in Tithe-silvered plate, the Houses' sworn sword. Not harvestable beyond belongings.

harvest.note: His signet and a few buckles of fine silver. His body is not harvestable.

monsters.name: Herald of Mab-Iselde
monsters.blurb: A tall, gloved fey in frost-silk who arrives politely in a crisis with a bargain already drawn up.

harvest.note: A herald that leaves in a hurry leaves a glove behind; one that is slain leaves only frost.

gather.cond: Only in streets split open by roots and brambles.
gather.riskWhy: Thornlings nest in the same briar patches.

gather.cond: Low brambles fruiting along kerbs and between market paving, late summer to first frost.
gather.riskWhy: Thornlings shelter in the same brambles; otherwise the squares are quiet.

gather.cond: In leaf-choked gutters and drains after rain; a failed check by 5 picks gutter cap instead.
gather.riskWhy: Cobblevine lies under the paving beside the choked drains.

gather.cond: Spreading from window boxes across sills, ledges and balconies in streets still half lived-in.
gather.riskWhy: Grows in plain sight on half-lived-in streets; a stray thornling at worst.

gather.cond: On the bell-frames of standing belltowers the roots have reached; a 30-foot climb (DC 12 Athletics).
gather.riskWhy: Canopy lurkers and threadwalkers like a high, quiet belfry.

gather.cond: Smoked out of bee colonies in the rafters of roofless houses; bring a smoking torch.
gather.riskWhy: Angry bees and rotten floorboards; a canopy lurker sometimes dens in the same loft.

gather.cond: Under young oaks that have heaved up the paving; leach them in water before eating.
gather.riskWhy: Rootwolves and bramble boars root for the same acorns at dusk.

gather.cond: In churchyards and walled gardens gone to seed.
gather.riskWhy: Quiet walled gardens; a thornling in the hedge at worst.

gather.cond: Choking the basins of silted fountains and horse-troughs.
gather.riskWhy: Cobblevines favour the damp stone around fountains.

gather.cond: On the wild briars that have swallowed hedges and railings; sweetest after the first frost.
gather.riskWhy: Thornlings nest in the briars, and boars come for the fallen hips.

gather.cond: Where roots have lifted old paving.
gather.riskWhy: Overgrown ruins attract thornlings and rootwolves.

gather.cond: Where old cellars and graves have been split open by growth; best at dawn.
gather.riskWhy: Cellars and graves hold loamborn and the odd charnel mound.

gather.cond: On brambles spilling over fallen walls and courtyards.
gather.riskWhy: Thornlings roll out of the briars; a rootwolf may be nosing about.

gather.cond: Along collapsed drains and sunken lanes after rain.
gather.riskWhy: Loamborn rise from wet rubble; cobblevine waits in the drains.

gather.cond: Scraped from the louvres of collapsed belltowers; the stairs are gone (DC 13 Athletics to climb).
gather.riskWhy: Canopy lurkers sleep in broken belfries, and a fall from the frame is a long one.

gather.cond: In the roof-beams of gutted halls and chapels, where the bees have had years undisturbed.
gather.riskWhy: Old colonies are large and angry, and the beams are where canopy lurkers rest.

gather.cond: Run wild from old cloister and chapel herb-beds.
gather.riskWhy: Thornlings and the odd loamborn haunt the old cloister gardens.

gather.cond: On old barrels and beams in flooded or root-split cellars; bring a light.
gather.riskWhy: Root-split cellars are where loamborn rise and charnel mounds sleep.

gather.cond: In abandoned guard-posts and barracks stores; about half the tins are still dry.
gather.riskWhy: Old barracks draw rootwolves, and drowned legionaries walk the lower posts.

gather.cond: Under old alders where roots tangle over buried stone.
gather.riskWhy: Old alders are watched by their guardians.

gather.cond: Under the oaks where the wood meets the old streets.
